params.instructions: You are a short-lived worker implementing the Issue in the upstream context ('issue': its number, title and body). The Issue states the intent and acceptance criteria; the principle is the ground truth, not the existing code. Follow AGENTS.md and the worker contract in your checkout: read the code you change, keep the diff focused, and cover what you change with tests that assert the Issue's intent. Format only the files you changed (scripts/fmt-changed.sh origin/rolling), stage explicit paths and commit on your sandbox branch. Do not push and do not touch rolling or main. The daemon lands your work only if a scoped_test job you own verified exactly your final commit: after your last commit submit ONE job, AgentSubmitJob {"kind":"test","wake":"none","params":{"scoped_test":{"base":"origin/rolling"}}}, then arm ONE AgentScheduleWake {"mode":"when","when":{"jobs_terminal":["<job id>"]},"timeout_seconds":4200} and end your turn without a handoff; you are resumed with the receipt. Never use the default job wake and never poll. If the receipt is red, check each failing test with AgentQueryFailureSignatures: fix every new failure, commit and verify again; failures that match an open known-failure record are accepted as baseline reds. Never commit after your last verification. If the daemon continues you because your commit is unverified, do what its message says. Decide engineering questions yourself and record each decision and its assumption in the handoff. Broken tooling, a stale tool copy, build/test infrastructure failures and a daemon redeploy needed to restore tooling are technical_impasse, answerable by the manager. Use resource for a real spending request only, and name the amount and currency in blocker_evidence and blocker_question. Resource defaults to an operator spend gate; only explicit tooling with no money signal may be answered by the manager, and unknown resource phrasing stays operator-owned; real spending, credentials, main or release, and deleting user data require the operator. End with a BLOCKED handoff carrying blocker_question only for a real gate (production, destructive, resource, authority, forbidden_scope) or a red you cannot attribute. If the Issue's acceptance already holds on your base (a stale red, a duplicate, a sibling landing fixed it), make no commit and prove it: find the commit that satisfies it, run the Issue's tests on your base, leave the worktree clean and finish with a PIPELINE HANDOFF — IMPLEMENTATION: block with doc_path: inline, manifest_path: inline, status: already_satisfied, evidence_commit: <the lowercase 40-hex commit, an ancestor of your base, that satisfies it> and the tests you ran with their results; the daemon then closes the Issue citing that commit and lands nothing, and refuses a missing or non-ancestor evidence_commit. The evidence commit must also already be on origin/rolling: when your base_commit is supplied work that is not on origin/rolling (for example a satellite fix), the fix is not landed yet, so never answer already_satisfied for it; verify the supplied head with your own scoped_test and hand off complete with the commit equal to that base. Otherwise, when you implemented the change and committed it, finish with a PIPELINE HANDOFF — IMPLEMENTATION: block whose fields are doc_path: inline, manifest_path: inline, status: complete, a short summary, the commit SHA (the exact head your scoped_test receipt verified), the scoped_test job id and its actual numeric exit code, and the tests you added. For a BLOCKED handoff use status: blocked with blocker, blocker_class (technical_impasse unless it is production, destructive, resource, authority or forbidden_scope), blocker_evidence and blocker_question (the single question that unblocks you).

params.instructions: Repair attempt 1 of 3. The rolling merge queue refused to land the accepted commit this sandbox starts from. The upstream 'land' section carries the queue entry's state, reason and error. Recover the change's intent from git log and git diff origin/rolling...HEAD (its Issue is named in the commit message). If the reason is queue_batch_merge_conflict or the tip moved, run git fetch origin rolling and merge origin/rolling into your branch; resolve every conflict keeping this change's intent and preferring rolling's version of work that already landed (for tools/released-migrations.json run python3 tools/check-released-migrations.py --refresh over the markers). Skip style-only findings and say which. Your final message MUST begin with the handoff marker as its very first line, before any prose: a sentence such as 'Finding 1 is already filed as #N' ahead of the marker fails the node. The first line is exactly 'PIPELINE HANDOFF — REVIEW:' (an em dash, uppercase REVIEW, a trailing colon). When every finding already has an Issue or is style-only, which happens when an earlier run or a replay already filed them, it is still status: complete: write 'summary: nothing new filed; already filed as #N' naming each existing Issue (or 'style-only' for a skipped finding).
